generalfeedback.text:
The vector \(\vec{v} = ({@vx@}, {@vy@})\) means:
\(\Delta x = {@vx@}\) (horizontal component)
\(\Delta y = {@vy@}\) (vertical component).
For example, starting at the origin \((0,0)\), the end point should be at \(({@vx@}, {@vy@})\).

hint.text: The vector components are the differences: dx = end_x - start_x, dy = end_y - start_y.
You can place the start point anywhere — only the direction and magnitude matter.

truefeedback.text:
Correct! Your vector has the right components.

{@feedback_msg@}

falsefeedback.text:
The vector components do not match. Remember: \(\Delta x = \text{end}_x - \text{start}_x\) and \(\Delta y = \text{end}_y - \text{start}_y\).

{@feedback_msg@}
